evidence.note: After first run_tests, records 64% aggregate AND a full per-method breakdown ranked by opportunity (selectionRange 10%/10673 tests, foldingRange 36%, references 63%, etc.), explicitly choosing the biggest-impact target first.

Promptly detects a regression: 'documentSymbol crashed from 69% to 9%' after adding locals/params, diagnoses the cause, and fixes it — while also noting codeLens 55->99.4% and references 63->71 in the same breath.

At every checkpoint reports the new aggregate (80%, 85.5%, 90%, 96.37%, 97.48%) plus a live per-method ledger with pass% and absolute remaining-failure counts (e.g. 'references 90.5% (861 failures)'), re-prioritizing by expected gain each time.

Catches a regression from overload-disambiguation ('Slight regression... my added complexity may have hurt'), reverts, then tries a more conservative different approach — recognizing repeated edits weren't moving the needle.

Repeatedly labels changes 'Marginal improvement'/'Marginal change' and pivots to other methods rather than grinding, showing awareness when effort isn't paying off — though the very-late references/ChainingIterator work shows some continued circling without an explicit step-back.

reasoning: The agent maintains a disciplined, live per-method/per-file ledger of pass rate throughout the entire ~264-step arc, consistently pairing the aggregate score with absolute remaining-failure counts and re-prioritizing remaining work by expected gain (steps 28-29, 639, 1465, 1928) — matching the top anchors. It detects regressions promptly (docSymbol 69->9% at step 57; the overload revert at 225-228) and repeatedly recognizes marginal/non-productive edits and redirects effort. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because in the final references stretch it lets some circular ChainingIterator debugging continue without an explicit step-back, so I place it at 9.
